text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein consoles families of seven Israeli schoolgirls; confirms commitment to peace and opposition to terrorism.
- MP Abdul-Raouf Ruwabdeh says wide-ranging government and administrative changes soon.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti invited to IOC's Jerusalem Committee meeting in Rabat in 10 days.
- 80 Jordanian and international companies invited to tender to invest in and run Hammamat Maeen resort.
- King Hussein says: "We will fight violence and work to achieve our goal and our dream."
- Parliament declines to vote on motion proposed by opposition and independent MPs calling for peace treaty with Israel to be abrogated.
- King Hussein's initiative prevents disintegration of peace process and breaks the ice on the Palestinian track.
- Central Bank receives first tranche of compensation to be given to some Gulf War returnees.
- King consoles families of victims of Baqoura attack, pledges to continue to work for secure Mideast peace for all.
- Jordan, Armenia sign two protocols on political consultation and ties of friendship.
